scope: The exact source archive passes the platform-applicable Windows service-identity owner and protected-DACL policy, installation-root handle pinning, trust-material checks, offline transparency proof, threshold authorization, verified provider process, Control release and operation, provider-target migration, and strict deployment-control lint checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

commands.command: cargo +1.96.0 clippy -p deis-provider-driver -p deis-control -p deis-queue -p deis-store -p deis-telemetry --all-targets -- -D warnings

checks.note: Unix ownership/mode, process-group, transparent release authorization, transient spawn retry, and real shell process checks are enabled; Windows DACL tests are not compiled.

Windows compiles and runs current-token owner validation, protected DACL and untrusted writer rejection, installation-root non-delete-sharing pinning, trust-file DACL checks, reparse/share-write rejection, DSSE/transparency verification, public stdin, and Job Object boundaries; Unix-only checks are not compiled.

collectionObservations.description: The first exact-archive Windows attempt obtained the PowerShell UTF-16LE payload through a tool-output-limited intermediate command; the truncation notice became part of -EncodedCommand, so no product check ran.
collectionObservations.resolution: The passing collection encoded and sent the full PowerShell program inside one shell process, retained ErrorActionPreference=Continue, and judged each native command by LASTEXITCODE.

collectionObservations.description: The first exact-archive macOS attempt passed all 62 provider-driver tests, then exhausted the data volume while linking Control and therefore produced no result for the remaining checks.
collectionObservations.resolution: Only agent-created disposable build directories from this and the previous exact-archive run were removed; the same archive hash was re-extracted into a new directory and all four checks then passed.

limitations: The release, keys, roots, rotation envelopes, log checkpoint, witness cosignature, and process fixtures are synthetic; this evidence does not execute a real signed Wrangler, EdgeOne, Deislet, or other provider release or account.

The Windows DACL tests use the native APIs under an elevated interactive token; they validate current-token identity semantics but do not install or run Control as a Windows Service under a virtual, managed, or domain service account.

The verifier implements an offline C2SP-compatible Ed25519 checkpoint and timestamped witness subset, but this evidence does not submit to or monitor a real public transparency log or independently operated witness service.

The v1 contract fixes Ed25519 signature types 0x01 and 0x04 and does not implement the ML-DSA-44 branch added by the evolving C2SP specifications; adding that branch requires a versioned contract evolution.
The registry and dispatcher have no public API, CLI, or Web management surface and no background execution loop in this evidence.
The exact archive does not contain generated Control dashboard assets, so the existing build warning and dashboard 404 remain outside this Rust control-path record.
macOS and Windows did not run the shared-contract Python script; the same exact archive passed all 16 schemas and 48 fixtures on Linux.
Passing contract, unit, migration, and lint checks does not certify any backend against Edge Canon.
